title: Salwa and the River That Argued
logline: Salwa fights Basira until they discover they were always the same water.
story: Certain they were opposites and enemies, Salwa, who carried journeyer, horsewoman, ran headlong against Basira, who was inner sight, insight. Each tried to push the other back uphill, and they struggled until both were spent and still. In that stillness Salwa noticed they had pooled together and could no longer tell which water had been which. What Salwa had fought so hard in Basira was only the part of Salwa that had never been lived. Joined, they became a river wide enough to carry them both.
moral: What you fight hardest in another is most often the unlived part of yourself.
